stories.headline: Israel election paradox as parties winning no seats could decide who forms government
stories.title: Israel election paradox as parties winning no seats could decide who forms government
stories.summary: Israel's upcoming elections are poised to be dramatically influenced by smaller parties struggling to surpass the 3.25 percent voting threshold. Their performance could tip the scales between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition and the opposition. Historical patterns reveal how these parties, despite failing to secure seats, can pivotally alter political landscapes, emphasizing their crucial role in shaping the next government.

stories.headline: Sheikh Hasina calls Rahman’s BRICS Summit absence ‘counterproductive’
stories.title: Sheikh Hasina calls Rahman’s BRICS Summit absence ‘counterproductive’
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14 : Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's decision to skip the BRICS summit in India was "immature" and damaged Bangladesh's national interest, former premier Sheikh Hasina has said, warning that foreign policy driven by personal reactions or short-term political calculations is inherently counterproductive. In an exclusive interview with PTI, Hasina said Bangladesh's participation at the summit of the influential grouping could have opened up new opportunities for the country's economic and social development, but that chance was lost. The former Bangladesh prime minister said if her presence in New Delhi was the reason behind Rahman's refusal to attend the summit, it was very unfortunate, as relations between two countries cannot be determined by personal considerations or political sensitivities involving one individual. Questioning Rahman's decision, Hasina said that a responsible government should "open doors for the country, not close them." New Delhi had extended an invitation to Bangladesh Prime Minister Rahman for the BRICS summit in his role as the current chair of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation). However, Rahman opted out of the summit, which took place in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. "It was deeply unfortunate that Bangladesh chose not to participate. In my view, it was an immature decision and one that did not serve Bangladesh's national interest," Hasina said. "BRICS is not simply a diplomatic gathering. It brings together major emerging economies and creates opportunities for cooperation in trade, investment, infrastructure, technology and development. By participating, Bangladesh could have gained valuable experience and opened new opportunities for its own economic and social development. That opportunity was lost," she said. The former prime minister said foreign policy cannot be conducted through personal reaction or short-term political calculation. "India is our closest neighbour and an important historic partner, but BRICS engagement is also about Bangladesh's own place in the international community," she noted. The 78-year-old Hasina, living in Delhi since she left Bangladesh following the collapse of her government in August, 2024 in the face of a massive anti-government agitation, also recalled, how then prime minister Ziaur Rahman visited New Delhi in 1979 even when she was staying in India. "After the assassination of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, along with members of my family on August 15, 1975, and the killing of the four national leaders inside Dhaka Central Jail on November 3, Ziaur Rahman came to power through an unconstitutional process," Hasina said in response to written questions. "Yet when he visited Delhi in 1979, I was living in Delhi. When he travelled to London in 1980, I was also in London. My presence in either city did not prevent him from travelling there," she said. "So why should my presence in Delhi prevent Ziaur Rahman's son, Tarique Rahman, from coming to India today? What is the real reason behind such a decision," she asked. "Relations between two countries cannot be determined by personal considerations or political sensitivities involving one individual," she stressed. Hasina also highlighted how her government's foreign policy approach helped Bangladesh's economic growth. "During my tenure, we maintained strong relations with India while also expanding cooperation with China, Russia, Japan, the United States, Europe and many other partners," she said. "Friendship with one country never required hostility towards another. Bangladesh needs a mature, balanced and confident foreign policy. A responsible government should open doors for the country, not close them," she said. The India-Bangladesh relations came under some fresh strain after Hasina held a virtual media interaction in New Delhi on August 5. Following the event, Dhaka reiterated its demand for her extradition and even sought to link it with Rahman's planned trip to India. New Delhi sought to distance itself from the event, saying it neither played a role in it nor endorsed Hasina's comments. The former prime minister also attacked the Rahman government for its overall foreign policy direction, and said it should be "independent, balanced and guided by national interest." "The principle given by the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, remains the best guide: friendship to all, malice to none. India is Bangladesh's closest neighbour and historic friend from the Liberation War," she said. "China is also an important development partner. Japan, the United States, Europe, ASEAN and the Muslim world are all important to Bangladesh. The problem is not engagement with China or any other country. The problem begins when one relationship is used against another," she said. "It begins when anti-India rhetoric is encouraged for domestic politics. It begins when major decisions are taken without transparency," she added. The Awami League leader said Bangladesh is passing through a "grave national crisis as democratic space has been "closed". "The judiciary has been used for political revenge. Media freedom has been restricted. Law and order have weakened. Minorities feel unsafe. Extremist forces have regained space. The economy has suffered," she said. "This is no longer only an Awami League issue. It is a national crisis. One of the country's largest political forces has been banned. Its leaders are in jail or forced into hiding," she said. "Millions of its supporters have been denied normal political rights. A country cannot return to stability by excluding such a large section of its own people. The suffering is being felt across the country, but Awami League leaders, workers and supporters have faced an unprecedented burden of political persecution," she said. Hasina, without divulging specific details of her return to Bangladesh, said she is going back to restore democracy. "Thousands have been jailed, many more have been forced into hiding, and families have lost homes, jobs, businesses and livelihoods simply because of their political identity," she said. "My return is part of the struggle to restore democracy, voting rights and the rule of law. I want to stand beside the people of Bangladesh, fight for their rights, and help restore democracy, security and development in my country," she said. "The people of Bangladesh must be allowed to decide their own future through a free, fair and inclusive election. That is why my return will be significant. It will be a step towards returning Bangladesh to its people," she added. At the same time, she admitted that her return to Bangladesh could be risky as she was given a death sentence by a Bangladeshi court, but asserted that she was not afraid. "This is not the first time death has come close. In 1975, my father, mother, brothers and almost my entire family were murdered. In 1981, despite military rule and intimidation, I returned to Bangladesh. There have been repeated assassination attempts, including the August 21, 2004 grenade attack, as well as imprisonment, conspiracy and political persecution," the Awami League leader said. "The greater concern today is not personal safety. It is the destruction of justice in Bangladesh. A death sentence imposed through a politically motivated process, without a genuine opportunity to defend oneself, cannot be called justice," she said. PTI

stories.headline: Congress Deletes Post Targeting CJI Surya Kant; BJP Slams Party Over Judiciary Row
stories.title: Congress Deletes Post Targeting CJI Surya Kant; BJP Slams Party Over Judiciary Row
stories.summary: The Congress has come under fire after its Kerala unit posted a message on X calling for Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to resign over his remarks on law and order. The post was later deleted, but the BJP seized on it to attack the party. The Supreme Court Bar Association also condemned the message, saying it undermined the dignity of the judiciary. Congress distanced itself from the post, with spokesperson Pawan Khera saying the person responsible had been removed. The controversy comes as the INDIA bloc challenges Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

stories.headline: India's price pain meets double-digit villain
stories.title: India's price pain meets double-digit villain
stories.summary: Wholesale prices rose to 11.39% on-year in September, from 9.92% in August, official data released by the commerce and industry ministry on Wednesday showed, due to a sharp rise in fuel and power, food and manufactured product prices.A Reuters poll of economists had, earlier this month, estimated wholesale inflation at 10.18% for the month.Meanwhile, data from earlier this week showed that the country’s retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September 2026 from 4.83% in August, owing to a sharp rise in food prices, particularly vegetables.Also Read: India's retail inflation quickens to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, hits near two-year high Inflation in fuel and power rose to 25.85% in September from 22.93% in August, while inflation in manufactured products increased to 9.76% from 8.37%.Inflation in primary articles, which include food articles, non-food articles and minerals, rose to 8.67% from 7.76% over the same period.The wholesale food index, which includes food articles and manufactured food products, recorded inflation of 8.66% in September, up from 7.05% in August.Among the key drivers of wholesale inflation were mineral oils, food articles, crude petroleum and natural gas, coal and lignite, basic metals, chemicals, textiles, rubber and plastic products, and electrical equipment, the ministry said.Also Read: Double trouble at the dinner table: When will food prices normalise for Indians?An ET Online survey of economists from earlier this month, showed that food inflation is likely to remain elevated over the coming months, with some expecting it to rise to 7-8% over the next three to six months. While fresh Kharif arrivals and winter Rabi supplies could bring relief from late 2026 or early 2027, uneven monsoon rainfall, El Nino risks and higher energy and farm-input costs could prolong price pressures.Economists flagged El Nino and uneven monsoon rainfall as key risks to food inflation, warning that they could affect Kharif yields and delay Rabi sowing. ICRA’s Aditi Nayar and ANZ’s Dhiraj Nim had flagged to ET Online that below-average reservoir levels are a concern for winter crops, with the impact on food prices depending on crop output and adverse weather conditions.Higher global commodity prices and energy costs add to the pressure on food prices.Elevated crude oil prices can raise farm, irrigation and transportation costs, while higher liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices can increase fertiliser costs. India’s dependence on imported edible oils also leaves the category exposed to global price movements, while higher freight, packaging and crop-protection costs could add to the cost of bringing food to market.In early October, the RBI hiked benchmark repo rate to 5.5% in first such increase since February 2023, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra flagging “it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year.”The September WPI inflation data was released under the revised series, introduced in June with 2022-23 as the base year to better reflect the economy’s current structure. The new series expands the commodity basket to 957 items from 697 and includes newer energy sources such as solar, wind and nuclear electricity.

Economists flagged El Nino and uneven monsoon rainfall as key risks to food inflation, warning that they could affect Kharif yields and delay Rabi sowing.

ICRA’s Aditi Nayar and ANZ’s Dhiraj Nim had flagged to ET Online that below-average reservoir levels are a concern for winter crops, with the impact on food prices depending on crop output and adverse weather conditions.
Higher global commodity prices and energy costs add to the pressure on food prices.
Elevated crude oil prices can raise farm, irrigation and transportation costs, while higher liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices can increase fertiliser costs.

India’s dependence on imported edible oils also leaves the category exposed to global price movements, while higher freight, packaging and crop-protection costs could add to the cost of bringing food to market.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear plea on Delhi voter notice disclosure
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear plea on Delhi voter notice disclosure
stories.summary: Supreme Court to hear plea on Delhi voter notice disclosure
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court will hear a plea seeking disclosure of Delhi voters issued revision notices.
The case could shape safeguards and restoration procedures for previously enrolled electors.
The petitioners have also sought a mechanism to restore voters whose names were removed during the revision without requiring them to declare that they are applying for inclusion for the first time.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the petitioners, mentioned the matter before a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi on Wednesday.
Bhushan said the period for filing claims and objections had been extended until October 30, after which the final voter list would be published.
He said the Supreme Court had issued notice on the main petition last month and the matter was likely to be heard on October 30.
After Bhushan requested that the plea be heard before October 30, the bench advanced the hearing to October 28.
When he urged the court to hear it even earlier, the bench said, “We are thinking of passing an order that will take care of it.”
On September 26, the Election Commission extended the deadline for filing claims and objections in the ongoing revision by a month to October 30.
The final voter list is now scheduled to be published on December 4.
The Supreme Court had on September 22 agreed to hear the petition filed by Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri.

The petition also sought the disclosure of the criteria, definitions, parameters used by computer systems and operational guidelines governing the classification of voters under the category of “logical discrepancies”.

stories.headline: Delhi SIR case: Supreme Court assures to ‘take care of’ EC move to restore deleted voters as fresh voters
stories.title: Delhi SIR case: Supreme Court assures to ‘take care of’ EC move to restore deleted voters as fresh voters
stories.summary: The application has asked the court to direct the EC to frame an appropriate mechanism for restoration/inclusion of deleted voters without forcing them to apply as first-time voters
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court of India agreed to intervene for Delhi’s voters deleted from the electoral roll pursuant to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), and are now effectively being asked by the Election Commission of India to misrepresent themselves as fresh applicants by filling out Form 6 to restore their names on the voter list.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant was informed by advocates Prashant Bhushan and Neha Rathi, appearing for petitioners Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, that deleted voters seeking re-inclusion in the electoral roll are being compelled by the Election Commission (EC) to file a declaration that they had never voted before or face imprisonment.
Form 6, prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules of 1960, requires every applicant to affirm that they are “applying for inclusion in the electoral roll for the first time”.
“The EC should either allow them to file Form 8 [for shifted voters] or create a new form for voters deleted in the SIR,” Mr. Bhushan submitted.
He said the Delhi SIR case was listed on October 30.
But that would be too late, as the last date for filing claims and objections for the ongoing SIR was the same day.
The Chief Justice advanced the date of the hearing to October 28.
“We are thinking of passing an order which will take care of this issue,” Chief Justice Kant remarked.
The application has asked the court to direct the EC to frame an appropriate mechanism for restoration/inclusion of deleted voters without forcing them to apply as first-time voters.

During the enumeration phase of the SIR in Delhi, 47,56,722 electors, that is, 32.78% of the voters who existed prior to the start of the SIR, were excluded from the draft electoral roll under the category of ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate).
For any person on the ASDD list, the only mechanism for filing a claim for having their name restored in the voter list is through Form 6.

“This creates a fundamental anomaly as all these people were previously enrolled on the voter list but are now required to submit Form 6 and make a declaration that they are seeking inclusion in the electoral roll for the first time, which is factually incorrect and wholly inapplicable to their circumstances,” the application said.

stories.title: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court Advances Hearing After Plea Flags Deleted Voters Being Asked To Fill Form 6
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today advanced the date of hearing in Delhi SIR matter, after it was alleged that voters, whose names have been deleted pursuant to the SIR exercise, are being asked to fill Form 6 for re-inclusion of their names on the electoral roll.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi advanced the hearing date from October 30 to October 28, on hearing Advocate Prashant Bhushan.

When Bhushan urged that a hearing on October 28 might not make much of a difference as October 30 is the last date for correction of deletions, the CJI said, "we are thinking of passing an order that will take care of [all this]".
Bhushan was mentioning the application filed by transparency activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri in the pending petition against Delhi SIR.

stories.title: Meghalaya Cabinet Approves School Complex Rules to Streamline Admissions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: SHILLONG: The Meghalaya Cabinet has approved the Meghalaya School Education School Complex Rules, 2026, to link primary schools with nearby secondary and higher secondary institutions, aiming to simplify admissions and reduce repeated paperwork as students progress through school.

Announcing the decision after a Cabinet meeting, Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma said the state's school structure often created admission difficulties, as the number of institutions declined at higher levels of education.
Meghalaya has 9,244 lower primary schools, 2,396 upper primary schools, 1,755 secondary schools and 532 higher secondary schools.
Sangma said students often had to complete admission procedures multiple times, including in Classes.
I, VI, IX and XI, making the process inconvenient and contributing to admission bottlenecks.
Under the new framework, lower and upper primary schools will be linked with nearby secondary and higher secondary institutions designated as nodal schools.

The arrangement aims to facilitate transitions, including from Class V to VI and Class VIII to IX, without requiring students to repeatedly complete admission formalities or submit transfer certificates.
The Chief Minister clarified that participation would be voluntary and would not interfere with the functioning or decision-making powers of schools.
The government would approach institutions willing to join the initiative.

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi hints at next move in CEC-SIR row, says protests will continue
stories.title: Rahul Gandhi hints at next move in CEC-SIR row, says protests will continue
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13: Congress leader & Leader of Opposition, Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday indicated that the INDIA bloc would continue its campaign against the government over the functioning of the Election Commission (EC), but declined to disclose the opposition’s next move, saying he did not want to “spoil the surprise”. According to The Times of India, Gandhi made the remarks while addressing reporters at a joint briefing of opposition parties at his residence, where he hosted leaders for evening tea. He said the protests would continue until the opposition achieved its objective. “Sooner or later, whether tomorrow, the day after, in three months, six months, a year, or two years, it (protests) will not stop. It will reach the end goal. I cannot tell you exactly how we will get there, because that would spoil the surprise, and we want to maintain the excitement and sense of surprise for you and the country,” Rahul Gandhi said. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha asserted that the Congress-led INDIA bloc would sustain its campaign with the same energy, strength and unity with which it had mobilised against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Gandhi also expressed respect for the Supreme Court and Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, while making it clear that the opposition would continue its political campaign irrespective of the outcome of judicial proceedings. “Thank you to the Supreme Court—we have immense respect for the Supreme Court, the Chief Justice of India, and the Indian judicial system. They have a role to play, and we hope they will play it. However, we are political people; no matter what happens, or which institution plays a role or doesn’t, political resistance will continue, people’s resistance will continue, and it will triumph,” he said. Rahul Gandhi’s remarks came a day after he and 10 other opposition leaders approached the Supreme Court in the matter. The petition names the Election Commission, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as respondents. Gyanesh Kumar, who became Chief Election Commissioner in 2025 after serving on the Election Commission, has repeatedly faced allegations from opposition parties of favouring the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The allegations have been contested amid the wider political debate over the functioning and impartiality of the poll body. The latest developments have brought the Election Commission’s decision-making process and the SIR exercise under renewed political and judicial scrutiny, with the opposition signalling that its campaign will continue alongside the proceedings in the Supreme Court.
